summary: All five in-scope executor findings are real and share one root cause: correlation bindings are pushed into operands whose SPARQL semantics are bottom-up scope boundaries (sub-SELECT projections, MINUS right operands, OPTIONAL operands containing them), while the one place where pushed bindings ARE in scope (LATERAL substitution) is treated as a badly-designed leak. The design introduces one shared executor-side scope analysis (`BindingScopeAnalysis`: out-of-scope-for-correlation predicate, compatibility-selection-safe allowlist, LATERAL-substituted input names, nested-projection test) and makes three operators enforce it: `ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep` becomes the scope boundary for nested sub-selects (withholds non-projected incoming bindings, pre-binds projected names only when the body is selection-safe, filters results by compatibility), `LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep` uses a hash left-join with a residual condition for every out-of-scope right operand (fixing the REG 3.4.1 and the correlated MINUS leak) and excludes LATERAL-substituted names from its problem-variable set (fixing the pre-existing lateral()[2] / SPARQL12 tests()[6] compliance failures, which I traced to the branch's `whenWellDesigned` wrapper), and `MinusQueryEvaluationStep` restricts the right operand's input to the MINUS comparison domain. The EXISTS per-probe substitution stops at sub-select boundaries, the `minus-assured-shared` anti-join stops trusting the planner (validates assured-shared names, probes with the shared names only, never substitutes, falls back to a real `MinusQueryEvaluationStep`), and `HashJoinIteration` closes its left input when opening the right fails. The unbounded hash build side is a real resource problem but needs a spilling build store; I recommend deferring it as roadmap 4.7 work with a concrete outline.

findings.title: OPTIONAL with a condition over a sub-SELECT leaks the left row into the sub-select (REG vs develop)
findings.severity: S1 (wrong results, all stores, regression vs develop)
findings.rootCause: core/queryalgebra/evaluation/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/query/algebra/evaluation/impl/evaluationsteps/LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:95 `if (!leftJoin.hasCondition() && TupleExprs.containsSubquery(leftJoin.getRightArg()))` is the only path that evaluates a sub-select right operand independently (HashJoinIteration, BuildSide.RIGHT, :96-101). With a condition the step falls through to `standard` (:131) whose `evaluate` (:166-181) uses `LeftJoinIterator.getInstance(left, bindings, wellDesignedRightEvaluationStep)`; LeftJoinIterator.java:94/:103 calls `rightEvaluationStep.evaluate(leftBindings)` per left row, PostFilterQueryEvaluationStep wraps `wrapped.evaluate(leftBindings)`, and ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep.java:37 `qes.evaluate(bindings)` hands the whole left row to the sub-select body, so `?t :r ?x` is evaluated with the outer `?x` bound (x is NOT projected by the sub-select, so under SPARQL bottom-up semantics it is a fresh variable), `ORDER BY ?x LIMIT 1` selects among pre-filtered rows, and `COUNT(?o)` (GroupIterator.java ~299 `arguments.evaluate(parentBindings)`) counts only compatible rows. develop (git show 4354ff137b^2 …LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:46-53) returned the HashJoinIteration unconditionally before computing the condition (a different bug: it dropped the condition), so the branch's `!hasCondition()` guard plus `whenWellDesigned` (:183-185) is what makes conditioned OPTIONAL-over-sub-select correlated. Note the same leak exists for `OPTIONAL { {SELECT …} ?t :z ?y }` even without a condition because `TupleExprs.containsSubquery` (model/helpers/TupleExprs.java:51-80) stops at a Join, and the Join step only protects its *right* arg (JoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:80,159-162) — JoinIterator evaluates a sub-select *left* arg with the correlated row. That variant is only closed by finding 3.4.3's projection boundary.
findings.fix: (a) In `supply`, replace the `!hasCondition() && containsSubquery(rightArg)` branch with `BindingScopeAnalysis.isOutOfScopeForCorrelation(rightArg)` (= variable scope change || containsSubquery || containsDifferenceInCurrentScope, i.e. exactly JoinQueryEvaluationStep.isOutOfScopeForLeftArgBindings moved to the shared helper) and build `optimized = bs -> new HashJoinIteration(left, right, bs, true, contract, context, BuildSide.RIGHT, leftJoin, residual)` where `residual` is `null` without a condition, otherwise `new ScopedQueryValueEvaluationStep(leftJoin.getBindingNames(), condition).asPredicate()` (same predicate/error handling as PostFilterQueryEvaluationStep: a ValueExprEvaluationException counts as false). (b) Add an optional `Predicate<BindingSet> residualCondition` to HashJoinIteration (new constructor overload; existing constructors pass null). In `getNextElement` (HashJoinIteration.java:191-262), when `leftJoin && residualCondition != null`: for the current probe row iterate the candidate build rows, build the merged row, test the predicate, emit only passing rows, and track `currentScanElemMatched`; when the candidate iterator is exhausted without any passing row emit the bare probe row (SPARQL LeftJoin: μ1 survives alone iff no compatible μ2 satisfies expr). Inner joins ignore the parameter (or apply it as a plain post-filter). (c) Keep bottom-up semantics for badly-designed inputs: `whenWellDesigned` currently routes them to BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator, which is itself correlated (BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator.java:131/:140 `rightEvaluationStep.evaluate(leftBindings)`) and therefore leaks too. Replace it for out-of-scope right operands with a generic scope wrapper: evaluate `optimized` with `getFilteredBindings(bindings, problemVars)` (BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator.java:181-185) and wrap the result in a FilterIteration that drops rows incompatible with the input bindings and re-adds the problem variables (the logic of BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator.java:84-106, extracted to a small `ScopeFilteredIteration`/static factory). (d) `problemVars`/`optionalVars` must exclude LATERAL-substituted names (see finding 3.9-lateral); otherwise the hash path is skipped for LATERAL inputs. The hash left join is sound here because the right operand is evaluated once with the LeftJoin's own input bindings (never with left rows), and HashJoinBindingContract.from (cascades/HashJoinBindingContract.java) already gives lookup = assured∩assured and compatibility = possible∩possible with partial-key indexes, so a nullable shared binding cannot drop rows.

findings.title: MINUS right operand evaluated with correlated (out-of-scope) bindings, e.g. MINUS inside OPTIONAL
findings.severity: S1 (wrong results, all stores, pre-existing in develop)
findings.rootCause: MinusQueryEvaluationStep.java:93-102 passes the operator's full input `bindings` to the right operand: SPARQLMinusIteration via `DelayedEvaluationIteration(rightQes, bindings)` (:97) and AdaptiveMinusIteration.initialize `rightQes.evaluate(parentBindings)` (:254). For `?s :p ?z OPTIONAL { ?s :q ?y MINUS { ?y :r ?z } }` the correlated LeftJoinIterator hands `{s=a,z=z1}` to the Difference; the RHS `?y :r ?z` is evaluated with z pre-bound to z1 and yields nothing, so nothing is removed, although develop's `comparisonBindingNames` (:104-137, shared *output* names = {y}) correctly excludes z from the comparison domain. Pre-binding a variable into the RHS is a selection on that variable and is only equivalent to MINUS compatibility for variables in the comparison domain; z is not, so the pushdown is unsound. The Join step avoids this for its own right arg (`containsDifferenceInCurrentScope`, JoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:164-177) but LeftJoin does not, and any enclosing correlated operator can re-introduce it.
findings.fix: In `MinusQueryEvaluationStep.evaluate` compute `rightInput = comparisonBindingNames == null ? bindings : retain(bindings, comparisonBindingNames ∪ BindingScopeAnalysis.lateralSubstitutedNames(rightArg))` and pass `rightInput` to both the SPARQLMinusIteration delayed right evaluation and AdaptiveMinusIteration (store it instead of `parentBindings` for `rightQes.evaluate`). Pushing exactly the comparison names is sound: every MINUS-left row l carries μ(v) for those names (the left operand receives μ), so selecting RHS rows with r(v)=μ(v) or v∉dom(r) is precisely the compatible set; names outside the comparison domain are fresh variables in the RHS under bottom-up semantics and must not be constrained. LATERAL-substituted names are added because under LATERAL they are constants in the whole right-hand side (see 3.9-lateral). The `comparisonBindingNames == null` legacy constructors keep full pushdown (they also compare on all names, which is self-consistent). Optional hardening (4.6): if `!BindingScopeAnalysis.isCompatibilitySelectionSafe(rightArg)` push nothing; I do not recommend it by default because nested OPTIONAL/sub-select operands are already scoped by 3.4.1/3.4.3 and pushing nothing turns correlated MINUS into a full RHS scan per invocation.

files.change: Restrict the right operand's input bindings to comparisonBindingNames (+ lateral-substituted names); thread `rightInput` into both right-evaluation paths.

findings.title: EXISTS over a sub-SELECT leaks outer bindings (per-probe substitution descends into nested Projection scopes; sub-select step passes incoming bindings through)
findings.rootCause: Two cooperating leaks. (1) FilterIterator.java:361-369 `evaluateSubstitutedExists` clones the EXISTS body and runs `new BindingAssignerOptimizer().optimize(clone, null, bindings)`; BindingAssignerOptimizer.java:36-53 VarVisitor replaces every Var whose name is bound, including Vars inside a nested sub-select Projection (`?t :r ?x` becomes `?t :r 1` although x is not projected and is therefore a fresh variable inside the sub-select). It is reached for every body that is not compatibility-selection-safe (FilterIterator.java:442-475 excludes Projection) from both DefaultEvaluationStrategy.prepare(Exists) (:2112-2129) and the specialised semi-join path (:303-304). (2) Even with a scope-aware substitution the probe still calls `.evaluate(bindings)` on the compiled body (FilterIterator.java:368; MaterializedExistsFilterIteration probe/materialization :195/:307), and ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep.java:37 forwards the outer row into the sub-select body; GroupIterator ~299 evaluates the aggregate argument with `parentBindings`, so `COUNT(?o)` sees o pre-bound. This is the general mechanism behind 3.4.1 as well and is the 4.1 'one binding/scope analysis' item.
findings.fix: (a) ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep becomes the scope boundary for nested sub-selects. At construction compute (via BindingScopeAnalysis) `nested = isNestedProjection(projection)` (some ancestor other than QueryRoot/Slice/Distinct/Reduced/Order/DescribeOperator), `lateralNames = lateralSubstitutedNames(projection) ∩ projectedSourceNames`, `innerSafe = isCompatibilitySelectionSafe(projection.getArg())` and `projectedSource = projectedSourceNames(projection)` (elements whose target equals the source name). In `evaluate(bindings)`: if `!nested` keep today's behaviour; else `inner = retain(bindings, lateralNames ∪ (innerSafe ? projectedSource : ∅))`, evaluate `qes.evaluate(inner)`, and wrap ProjectionIterator (parentBindings = original `bindings`) in a FilterIteration that drops rows whose projected target values conflict with a value in `bindings` (compatibility on projected names). This implements 'sub-select evaluated independently, then joined on projected names' with bind-join pre-binding retained only where it is provably a selection. Top-level projections are untouched (external bindings are already substituted by BindingAssignerOptimizer in every pipeline; FedX does not run it and must keep the pass-through). (b) EXISTS substitution must stop at sub-select boundaries: add `BindingAssignerOptimizer.substituteInScope(TupleExpr, BindingSet)` (or a new ScopedBindingSubstitution visitor) that overrides `meet(Projection)`/`meet(MultiProjection)` to not descend; keep the shared optimizer's external-binding semantics unchanged. (c) In `evaluateSubstitutedExists` clone into a holder `new Exists(subQuery.clone())` and precompile `holder.getSubQuery()` so the clone has a parent and (a)'s `isNestedProjection` sees a Projection-rooted body as nested (today the clone is a parentless root). Same holder idea is used for LATERAL (3.9-lateral). (d) Follow-up perf item (not required for correctness): with (a) a Projection-rooted EXISTS body is independent of the outer row, so FilterIterator.supplyMaterializedExistsSemiJoin could stop declining `subquery-scope-boundary`/`unprojected-correlation-reference` for such bodies and materialise once instead of probing per row.

findings.title: `minus-assured-shared` anti-join hint trusted blindly: hinted body probed with full substitution (NOT EXISTS semantics), materialised with referenced-name parameters
findings.severity: S1 (wrong results when the packed planner chooses the anti-join; executor-level)
findings.rootCause: FilterIterator.java:249-256: `assuredSharedMinus` only relaxes the root scope-change check (`containsVariableScopeChange(subQuery, true)`); after that the MINUS body is treated exactly like an EXISTS body: `requiresPerProbeExistsSubstitution` (:257) is true for any FILTER/EXTENSION/PROJECTION/LEFT_JOIN/GROUP body, the probe is `evaluateSubstitutedExists` (:358-369) which substitutes ALL left-row bindings (including `?o`, which is out of scope inside a MINUS operand), and `correlationCandidates`/`materializationParameterBindingNames` (:265-280) include every variable referenced in the body (VarNameCollector), so the materialisation path also pre-binds `?o`. Result: `Filter(left, Not(Exists(?s :q ?v FILTER(?v=?o))))` removes the row (a :q o1 matches with o substituted) while `Difference(left, same body)` keeps it. The planner side (PackedLogicalRuleProgram.java:381-421, safeCorrelatedMinusProbe :604-627) accepts such bodies (wp2, finding 3.2.1); the LMDB e2e repro passed only because the planner happened to keep Difference.
findings.fix: Executor implements MINUS semantics for this kind and validates the hint (roadmap 4.2 'rewrite re-checked at execution', 4.6 fail-safe). In `supplyMaterializedExistsSemiJoin` when `assuredSharedMinus`: (1) `shared = outputs(filter.getArg()) ∩ outputs(subQuery)` (use MinusQueryEvaluationStep's actualOutputBindingNames logic, minus constant var names); validate `!shared.isEmpty()`, `filter.getArg().getAssuredBindingNames().containsAll(shared)` and `subQuery.getAssuredBindingNames().containsAll(shared)`; (2) probe function = `row -> existsArg.evaluate(retain(row, shared))` — never `evaluateSubstitutedExists`; (3) `correlationKeyBindingNames = shared`, `materializationParameterBindingNames = ∅` (materialise the body once, unbound; `matches()` then is exactly MINUS compatibility on assured shared names, and dom(l)∩dom(r)≠∅ holds because shared is assured on both sides); (4) `strategyMode`: if `BindingScopeAnalysis.isCompatibilitySelectionSafe(subQuery)` honour the planned mode, else force MATERIALIZED (a restricted probe is a selection only for selection-safe bodies); (5) if validation fails, do not fall back to the plain FilterIterator (that is NOT EXISTS): return `bs -> new MinusQueryEvaluationStep(arg, existsArg, filter.getArg(), subQuery).evaluate(bs)` — the node carries the semantic kind, so a real MINUS operator is always the correct fallback — and record disposition `declined:minus-hint-invalid`. Keep `semanticKind()` telemetry in MaterializedExistsFilterIteration.

Expose (package/@InternalUseOnly) the shared-output-name computation for reuse by the minus-mode validation.

findings.title: HashJoinIteration leaks its left input when opening the right input throws
findings.severity: S2 (resource leak / cursor leak on LMDB reader pool)
findings.rootCause: HashJoinIteration.java:145-146: `this.leftIter = left.evaluate(bindings); this.rightIter = right.evaluate(bindings);` in the constructor; a QueryEvaluationException from the second call propagates before the object exists, so `handleClose` (:264-311) can never close `leftIter`. All production callers (JoinQueryEvaluationStep :77/:83, LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep :98, FederationEvaluationStrategy :823, BoundedHashJoinIteration super call :670) are affected; AdaptiveHashLeftJoinIteration avoids it only because it owns its inputs.
findings.fix: In the contract-aware constructor open the left input, then open the right input inside try/catch(RuntimeException|Error): on failure close the left input (adding a close failure as suppressed) and rethrow. Roadmap 4.7's lazy opening (open both inputs in setupHashTable under a lifecycle lock, as AdaptiveHashLeftJoinIteration does) is the fuller form; it is not needed for this leak and changes close-before-first-next semantics, so keep it as a follow-up.

files.change: Guarded right-input opening with suppressed-exception cleanup of the left input.

additionalTests: Left close failure during cleanup is attached as suppressed to the original exception; left-open failure does not attempt to close a right input.
existingTestsAtRisk: None expected (HashJoinIterationTest, JoinMetricsTrackingTest, AdaptiveHashLeftJoinLifecycleTest use successful inputs).

findings.title: Hash-join build side is drained without any bound or spill
findings.severity: S2 (unbounded memory for out-of-scope joins that cannot fall back to a correlated algorithm)
findings.rootCause: HashJoinIteration.java:344-364 setupHashTable / :369-375 `drain` buffer the whole build input into an in-memory Collection (makeIterationCache :657-659) with no limit. Only the LeftJoin UNION path bounds it (LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep BoundedHashJoinIteration :665-687 + fallback to LeftJoinIterator) — a fallback that is only valid for compatibility-selection-safe right operands; for the out-of-scope operands that force a hash join (sub-selects, scope changes, MINUS-containing groups, and after 3.4.1 every conditioned OPTIONAL over them) no correct fallback exists, so a bound alone would just fail the query.
findings.fix: Roadmap 4.7: give HashJoinIteration a bounded, spilling build store. Extract MinusQueryEvaluationStep's RightSpill/spilled-row scanning (:178-400, temp file + per-left-block rescan) into a shared `SpillableBindingSetStore` in evaluation/iterator; in HashJoinIteration, when the build collection exceeds `org.eclipse.rdf4j.query.algebra.evaluation.hashjoin.maxBuildRows` (default 1_000_000, same convention as the other properties), switch to block nested-loop over the spilled build rows per probe block (correct for inner and left joins and independent of correlation semantics). Publish `actualCostPeakMemoryRows`/spill counters so the cost model (wp2/LEO) learns the switch. Keep the existing `add`/`makeIterationCache` hooks so BoundedHashJoinIteration keeps working.

files.change: Bounded build with spill-to-disk block nested loop.

additionalTests: Build side > limit: results identical to unbounded hash join for inner and left joins, with partial-key build rows and cross products; spill file removed on exhaustion and on early close; close during spill scan.
existingTestsAtRisk: HashJoinIterationTest, AdaptiveHashLeftJoinLifecycleTest, MinusQueryEvaluationStepTest spill tests (refactor of RightSpill).
findings.risk: Medium (I/O, lifecycle, cancellation); no correctness change when under the limit.
findings.recommendationReason: Real robustness gap but not a wrong-result bug; needs a spilling store and its own ExecPlan (Routine D). Land after 3.4.1 raises hash-join usage.

findings.title: LATERAL { OPTIONAL { SELECT … LIMIT 1 } } returns 1 row instead of 3 (compliance lateral()[2] and SPARQL12 tests()[6], all stores)
findings.severity: S1 (wrong results, all stores, introduced on this branch before the merge)
findings.rootCause: Both failing ids are the same query (`?s ex:predicate ?o LATERAL { OPTIONAL { SELECT * { ?s rdfs:label ?label } LIMIT 1 } }`; JUnit dynamic-test indices are 1-based: LateralTest.tests() #2 = testLateralWithOptional, SPARQL 1.2 manifest-all = 4 aggregates + lateral-02 'LATERAL join with OPTIONAL' = #6). LateralQueryEvaluationStep.java:90-92 evaluates the right arg per left row with the LATERAL input names {s,o} (substitution semantics: those names are in scope inside the right-hand side). The right arg is LeftJoin(SingletonSet, Slice(Projection)); LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.supply computes optionalVars = vars(rightArg) − bindingNames(leftArg=SingletonSet) = {s,label} (:81-92,:133-164) and the branch-added `whenWellDesigned` (:98-101,:183-195) sends any input binding `s` to BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator with problemVars={s}: the SingletonSet and the sub-select are evaluated WITHOUT s (BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator.java:73,:131), `LIMIT 1` returns the store's first label (subject1/'Label 1'), the joined row is then rejected as incompatible with the input for subject2/subject3 (:84-86) and, because the join 'succeeded', the left row is never emitted either — exactly 1 row (subject1) instead of 3. develop returned the HashJoinIteration unconditionally for a sub-select RHS (git show 4354ff137b^2 …:46-53), which passed the row with s bound into the sub-select, so the test passed there. Under LATERAL semantics the substituted variables are constants inside the right-hand side and can never be badly-designed problem variables; the LeftJoin step has no way to know that today, and the cloned right arg (LateralQueryEvaluationStep.java:101-104) has no parent chain to discover the enclosing Lateral.
findings.fix: (a) `BindingScopeAnalysis.lateralSubstitutedNames(TupleExpr node)`: walk `getParentNode()`; whenever the current node is the right arg (or inside it) of a `Lateral`, add `lateral.getRightInputBindingNames()`; when passing through a Projection/MultiProjection keep only names that are projected source names (defensive; the HiddenLateralBindingRenamer already renamed hidden names). (b) LateralQueryEvaluationStep.prepareRight (:95-105): after cloning/renaming, attach a synthetic parent `new Lateral(new SingletonSet(), scopedRight, rightInputBindingNames)` before `strategy.precompile(scopedRight, context)` so the parent walk works for the clone too (the non-cloned `right` already has the real Lateral parent). (c) LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.supply: `optionalVars.removeAll(BindingScopeAnalysis.lateralSubstitutedNames(leftJoin))` before constructing the step, so `isWellDesignedFor` ignores them; the well-designed path (hash for the sub-select RHS, LeftJoinIterator otherwise) then passes s into the RHS, and with 3.4.3's projection boundary the Projection pushes `s` because it is a lateral-substituted projected source name. (d) Same set feeds MinusQueryEvaluationStep (3.4.2) and ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep (3.4.3). This is the 4.1 roadmap item in executor form: one analysis answering 'which incoming names are in scope by substitution' for all operators.

Semantics decision needed with the spec owners: whether SPARQL 1.2 EXISTS substitution pushes *projected* variables into a non-monotone sub-select (LIMIT/aggregate) or the sub-select is evaluated independently and joined (design chooses the latter; one-line switch in ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep for EXISTS context if the former is required).
openQuestions: SPARQL 1.2 substitute() semantics for EXISTS over a sub-select whose *projected* variable is bound in the outer row and whose body is not monotone (`EXISTS { SELECT ?x WHERE {…} ORDER BY ?x LIMIT 1 }`): substitution into the body vs independent evaluation + compatibility. The repro tests only cover non-projected variables; the design picks compatibility (consistent with Join/LeftJoin hash paths) and pins it with a test — confirm against the spec text before landing 3.4.3.

Should the projection boundary also withhold correlation bindings from top-level projections when the strategy is used without the BindingAssignerOptimizer (FedX, direct strategy.evaluate callers)? Design keeps pass-through for top-level projections to preserve external-binding semantics; verify with FedX compliance.

Perf envelope of 3.4.3 for EXISTS over LIMIT/aggregate sub-selects (per-probe unbound evaluation): decide whether to widen FilterIterator.supplyMaterializedExistsSemiJoin to Projection-rooted bodies (materialise once) in the same change or as a follow-up.

3.4.2 hardening: push nothing into a MINUS RHS that is not compatibility-selection-safe (fail-safe) vs push comparison names always (perf). Design: push comparison names; revisit if a correctness case surfaces that 3.4.1/3.4.3 do not already cover.
